subject: Medisolutions follow-up: prompt/output PII and retention clarifications
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medisolutions.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T15:10:00-04:00
Subject: Quick follow-up / call notes + specific PII questions

Hi Lena — thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and a few specific questions so we can scope the right deployment and security posture: 

Summary / next steps we discussed:
- Primary use: model-assisted clinical suggestion generation for triage workflows (low-latency).
- Concern: any generated output that contains patient identifiers must be treated as PHI.
- Procurement: you mentioned an internal PO and a 60-day legal review.
- Ask: we’ll prepare a mutual action plan + SOC 2 artifacts.

Questions (to confirm configuration choices):
1) Are model outputs that include patient identifiers considered PHI for the purposes of retention and logging? If yes, would you prefer we disable output persistence entirely for the clinical routes or keep outputs for a short rolling window (e.g., 30 days) for debugging?
2) Residency: do you require data to be stored and processed only in US regions (no EU/APAC processing)?
3) Prompt logging: are you comfortable with redacted prompt logging (strip PHI/patient identifiers) or do you need prompt text never persisted in any logs for the clinical routes?
4) Key management: do you require customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for encryption-at-rest?
5) Audit logs: minimum retention for audit trail and compliance?

Attachments: I’ve attached the quick call notes (20270502-call-notes.pdf). We’ll also include a short config proposal once you confirm the three items above.

Example options we can implement quickly:
- Option A (fast): Hosted API + routing policy that disables output retention and enables prompt redaction for the "clinical_suggestions" route; US-only routing.
- Option B (recommended for compliance): Dedicated capacity with VPC peering + CMK; full audit logs retained (configurable), no prompt/output persistence for PHI routes.
- Option C (private): Private deployment inside your VPC (air-gapped) — we’ll coordinate on onboarding and SOC2 evidence exchange.

Please reply with short answers to Q1–Q3 and we’ll lock the config and draft the DPA redline for procurement.

Thanks,
Rafael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medisolutions.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: security@medisolutions.com, procurement@medisolutions.com
Date: 2027-05-02T18:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up / call notes + specific PII questions

Hi Rafael — thanks for the notes and the clear options. See answers inline below and attached our formal requirements PDF (Medisolutions_Data_Handling_Reqs.pdf).

Q1: Yes — any generated output that contains patient identifiers is considered PHI. We would prefer no persistence of those outputs by default. If there is a debug/evidence path, it must be explicit, time-limited to 30 days max, and available only to our approvers.

Q2: Residency: US-only processing/storage required for systems that may touch PHI. We cannot permit processing in EU/APAC for PHI workloads.

Q3: Prompt logging: we do not want full prompt text persisted for clinical routes. Redaction is acceptable if it is proven reliable; otherwise, prompts should not be stored.

Other items:
- Key management: we require customer-managed keys (AWS KMS CMKs) for any persistent storage of tokens or outputs related to PHI.
- Audit logs: we need immutable audit logs for 365 days; logs may be restricted to metadata only (timestamps, request ids) but must not include raw prompt/offending content.
- Compliance artifacts: please provide SOC 2 Type II report and encryption at rest documentation. We’ll need a short data flow diagram for our legal/security review.

We will route procurement once legal gets the DPA/redlines. I’ve attached our requirements doc for the intake.

Lena Ortiz
Head of Data & Security | Medisolutions Inc.
lena.ortiz@medisolutions.com
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medisolutions.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Fwd: Medisolutions reqs — need quick config + DPA redline

Marissa / Neha — forwarding Lena's reply and their attached requirements. Key asks: US-only residency for PHI, CMK required for PHI-at-rest, no persistence of PHI outputs (30-day exception only if explicitly approved), and audit logs retained 365 days (metadata-only).

Proposed immediate plan: 
- Draft MOP (mutual action plan) that lists milestones: config sign-off, DPA redline, SOC2 exchange, PO issuance, pilot (2 weeks), production deployment.
- Technical config (recommended): Dedicated capacity with VPC peering + CMK + route-level output persistence disabled for clinical_suggestions; enable metadata-only audit logs with 365-day retention.
- Fallback: If Dedicated timeline is too long, propose Hosted API with strict route-level controls + zero output persistence + VPC/VPN peering for ingestion.

Marissa — can you own the MAP and procurement coordination? I’ll prepare a first-pass DPA redline.
Neha — can you confirm the technical feasibility and whether our redaction pipeline is certified for PHI redaction (or whether we should mark redaction as insufficent and require no-persist)?

Also attaching: call notes and their PDF (see attachments). If we need to offer a credit to accelerate Dedicated capacity onboarding, say so.

Thanks — Rafael
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T09:23:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Medisolutions reqs — need quick config + DPA redline

Rafael / Marissa — quick notes from infra/security POV: 
- Confirmed: Dedicated capacity + VPC peering + CMK covers all asks and aligns with compliance. Private deployment is also possible but will add ~6–8 weeks.
- Audit logs: we can provide immutable metadata-only audit logs with 365-day retention and export to their S3 (read-only) bucket for legal hold. We will NOT store raw prompt text for the clinical_suggestions route if we configure "no_persist" on that route.
- Redaction: our automated PHI redaction is robust for many cases but not guaranteed for every custom identifier pattern; for full compliance we should treat outputs with patient identifiers as non-persistable unless Medisolutions explicitly accepts redaction caveats in the DPA.
- Deliverables I can attach to the MAP/DPA package: SOC 2 Type II redacted report, encryption docs, sample dataflow diagram. I’ve attached the internal PII spec we send to enterprise customers (redwood-pii-spec-2027-04.pdf).

Next steps: Rafael — please confirm whether we should propose Dedicated + CMK as the default option in the MAP (I recommend yes). Marissa — I can schedule a 30-minute technical Q/A with their SecOps to walk the configuration.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Security Engineering | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
